CAP_T|/CL170/sub: Crystalline waterproofing admixture with liquefying properties
CAP_T|/CL170/role: The liquid 2-in-1 for the concrete plant: a concrete plasticiser after DIN EN 934-2 (Table 2) with crystalline effect, dosed with the mixing water. Water saving up to 10 % gives a lower w/c ratio and a smoother consistency; the active ingredient grows crystals in the pores and heals cracks up to 0.4 mm. Suitable for drinking water after DVGW W 270 and W 347.

CA_STEPS|/planA/short: Exposure, water load and crack-width limits by the engineer; a recipe within the requirements of the data sheet; the component at least 15 cm thick.
CA_STEPS|/planA/overview: The planner and the structural engineer define the exposure classes, the water load and — decisive for the self-healing — the crack-width limits of the component: the crack expansion limitations must be complied with under any circumstances, contrary designs are verified after the corresponding verification and suitability. The concrete is a watertight concrete after DIN EN 206 / DIN 1045-2 within the requirements of the data sheet: cement ≥ 270 kg/m³ (CEM I), ≥ 290 (CEM II), ≥ 380 (CEM III/A; {CP360} also CEM III/B ≥ 400); w/c ratio < 0.55; fly ash ≤ 80 and granulated slag ≤ 100 kg/m³ added to the binder; grain size 16 mm, in exceptional cases 32 mm; component thickness not less than 15 cm.
CA_STEPS|/planA/points/0: concretes of exposure class XA3 (DIN EN 206-1 / DIN 1045-2) are excluded; CEM III/C cements are prohibited, CEM III/B for {CL170}, {CL210} and {CP350}
CA_STEPS|/planA/points/1: lignite fly ash is of limited suitability; as the share of Portland cement and the dosage fall, the crystallisation may slow down
CA_STEPS|/planA/points/2: unless otherwise agreed, the manufacturer is responsible for the concrete mix design; concrete ordered by properties after DIN EN 206 may contain admixtures after DIN EN 934-2 — without a CE mark the recipe would become a concrete composition and the responsibility passes to the customer
